minutes_text:
APPROVED by: Youth Commission on June 8th, 2021

  MINUTES
  Alhambra Youth Commission
  April 13th, 2021

The Alhambra Youth Commission was called to order at 6:00 pm on April 13th, 2021 via
teleconference and video conference.

Commission Members Present: Andrade, B. Gonzalez, V. Gonzalez, Munson, J. Quach, N.
Quach, Romano, Webster

Commission Members Absent: Cooper, Gutierrez, Luc, and Manuel

Also, present: Kyle Kim - Guest, Vincent Hon - Recreation Supervisor, Michael Macias –
Director of Parks & Recreation

IV.  Nominations and Election of President and Vice President of the Youth
  Commission
  Recreation Supervisor Hon discusses the nomination and election process for the
  President and Vice President of the Youth Commission. Mr. Hon begins to take
  nominations from the Commissioners present. Commissioner Nicolas Quach is
  elected President of the Youth Commission. Commissioners begin the nominations
  for Vice President of the Youth Commission. Commissioner Munson is elected
  Vice President of the Youth Commission.

V.  Discussion Regarding the Purpose of the Youth Commission – To Provide
  Educational and Service Experience for the Youth of the City by Actively
  Involving them in The Functions of The City Government and Solving the
  Community Oriented Problems of their Peers and Attendance

  Recreation Supervisor Hon discusses the role of the Youth Commission and their
  presence in the City. Mr. Hon states during the monthly meeting, commissioners
  are encouraged to brainstorm ideas and bring up topics to be prioritized. Mr. Hon
  discusses the importance of discussing the Youth Commissions short term goals;
  hence the need to focus on prioritized topics such as upcoming events. Mr. Hon
  states that these Youth Commission meetings are now mandatory and failure to
  attend 3 meetings can result in the commissioner being elected out of the group.

VI.  Discussion Regarding Arbor Day Activity, Ceremony and Tree Planting

  There are no oral communications at this time. Supervisor Hon begins to go over
  the Arbor Day event specifics. The event will be held Thursday April 29th, 2021, at
  2:30 pm. The ceremony will be approximately 15 minutes long. At the event, the
  youth Commission president; Commissioner N. Quach, will be speaking. Youth
  Commissioner N. Quach will prepare a 1–2-minute speech regarding Arbor Day
  and the meaning for being there. Commissioners possibly able to attend the event
  are J. Quach, Gonzalez, Andrade, Webster, Munson, Romano, N. Quach. Mr. Hon
  will reach out to the Commissioners not in attendance. The planting of the trees
  will take place a week prior on Wednesday April 21st at 12:00pm in Almanor Park.
   The Commissioners able to attend this are Commissioners J. Quach, N. Quach,
  Munson, Romano, and Webster. Supervisor Hon and the attending Youth
  Commissioners will meet at the recreation office located at Almanor Park. Mr.
  Hon begins to summarize the plans for the event with the Youth Commissioners.

VII.  Discussion Regarding Opportunities for Youth Involvement During Covid-19

  Supervisor Hon states the City is operating with the Covid regulations set by the
  Governor. Mr. Hon begins to list the events and opportunities that will be held and
  available this upcoming year. The first event will be May 31 – Memorial Day. Mr.
  Hon will be recording a video to present for Memorial Day consisting of
  interviews with local veterans and asks for some of the Youth Commission to
  volunteer to be a part of the video. The Commissioners interested in taking part of
  the project are; Commissioners Webster, Munson, J. Quach, B. Gonzalez, and V.
  Gonzalez. The next event will be the 8th grade graduation held at Alhambra Park
  on. The next event(s) will be movies and concert in the park, the concerts will be
  every Friday starting on July 2nd. Movies in the park will begin Saturday July 3rd
  and run every Saturday in July from 7:00pm-8:30pm. The next event will be the
  4th of July which will include of a 15–20-minute firework show starting at
  9:00pm. The next event will be Veterans Day in November and lastly the Holiday
  Home Decorating contest in December. Mr. Hon states that the following year, if
  health regulations permit it, we will be back to the normal event setups. Director
  Macias states that the City Council has approved a Rose Parade Float event. This
  will take place in December and will present a great opportunity for Youth
  Commissioners to participate and help in the decorating in a float which will take
  part in the Rose Parade. Commissioner N. Quach interjects with comments about
  reaching out to more youth to participate in the events aside from those in the
  Youth Commission. Mr. Hon states that many of these events are open to
  accepting volunteers and will discuss youth involvement projects further with
  Youth Commissioner President N. Quach.

VIII. Discussion Regarding a Youth Summit

  Recreation Supervisor Vincent Hon begins the discussion by stating the need to
  begin brainstorming ideas to hopefully hold a Youth Summit at the end of the year.
  Youth Commission President N. Quach present the idea of having a youth outreach
  project to better understand the youth of Alhambra. Mr. Hon suggests a
  questionnaire to be distributed to the commissioner’s high schools. Youth
  Commissioner Vice President Munson suggest a type of in person panel to better
  reach out to the youth and get them involved. Mr. Hon suggest a panel for a Q&A.
  Mr. Hon suggest doing a Youth Commissioner of the Year Award to be presented
  at the Youth Summit held at the end of this year. Commissioner Munson and N.
  Quach suggest a more open-ended award in its stead, such as Youth of the year or
  Activist of the Year. Director Macias adds that if the Youth Commission follows
  through with the more open-ended award, then the Youth Commission itself
  should be more involved with building up the criteria for this award.
  Commissioner Romano suggest promoting the youth summit and the youth award
  to the various schools in Alhambra as well as on various social media platforms.
  Commissioner Webster adds that during the youth summit there be a time slot to
  better promote the youth commission by highlighting the events and programs they
  take part in. Commissioner Webster asks what ages the youth summit will be open
  to as well as the age requirement to apply to take part in the youth commission.
   Recreation Supervisor Hon adds that there is a possibility for the group to grow
  and lead to more youth summits taking part in the year. Commissioner Munson
  adds the possibility doing a college preparedness seminar to discuss with students
  the importance of applying for scholarships and financial aid to alleviate some
  financial stress they may have about applying. He also notes needing a segment to
  discuss possible career paths with the youth as they reach the end of their time in
  school. Commissioner Munson also adds wanting to include the LGBTQ+ youth in
  our community with the youth commission.

IX.  Oral Communications

  There are no oral communications at this time.

X.  Commission Orals

  Commissioner B. Gonzales adds wanting to have local organizations participate by
  having them speak at the youth summit and provide sign up forms to get the youth
  involved in them. Commissioner B. Gonzales also adds the topic of creating an
  official Youth Commission Instagram as a means of promoting their events, what
  they do, and how to join. Commissioner J. Quach adds wanting to have a guest
  speaker attend a youth summit to speak about their field of expertise. Mr. Hon
  agrees with the idea of bringing on guest speakers and college prep speakers to
  review with students the college application process as well as explain the various
  financial aid and scholarship option there are.

XI.  Adjournment
  The meeting was adjourned at 7:30 PM
